items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Cal Tjader made the first recording of my tune entitled “The Cubano Chant,”

ctx.x: When you started putting your own trios together, I’m wondering when you started writing your own tunes, had that been something you were doing all along, or was it something that maybe when a record date opportunity came along that you wanted to then branch out and do your own?

Well as far as writing my own tunes, that started long before I came to New York City and long before I got a recording contract of my own. You know I wrote a few tunes that were recorded by other people. George Shearing recorded a few of my songs, and Cal Tjader made the first recording of my tune entitled “The Cubano Chant,” which is a pretty well known tune by now. But when I got my first recording contract, actually I made my first recording date under my own leadership, under my name, was around ‘55, long…
Oh yeah. Probably hard to keep a working group together for a long stretch of time given the nature of the business.
